body: I like this PR, hoping to get this in eventually
@lodekeeper  can you verify the soak result for this PR? It's deployed on feat1-sas on Hoodi since Oct 13. Check if there is any regression or error compared to unstable-sas.

I don't see any regression from this PR. feat1-sas has been running 4c98359 since Oct 13 08:29 UTC. I compared it with unstable-sas over the last 7h, since unstable restarted Oct 14 16:00:

- Both stayed synced the whole window, with the same head lag, 201 peers each and 6 reorgs each.
- Block became head: mean 1.62s vs 1.68s, p95 3.71s vs 3.77s. Received to verified: 0.30s vs 0.33s.
- Head votes 86.6% vs 86.6%, target votes 99.7% vs 99.8%.
- getBlobsV2 success_resolved: 1674 vs 1690.

Two differences come from the host, not this PR. All feat1 nodes run Node 26.3.0, while unstable runs 24.21:

- RSS is 19.5 GB vs 9.1 GB, but heap used is the same (~3.3 GB), and feat1-sas was already at 16-18 GB on its previous build.
- There were ~50 error logs in 7h: `uncaughtException: The operation was aborted` thrown from the libp2p dial queue abort path, plus 3 `recvmsg ECONNREFUSED`. Every feat1 node logs this, including the ones on an older branch, and feat1-sas logged it before this deploy too. unstable, beta and stable have none. The rate did go up from ~170/day on the previous v1.46 build to ~1000-1600/day now. Nothing in this PR touches dialing, so it's worth a separate look at Node 26 + libp2p.

The extra by_range errors on feat1-sas are correct rejections of requests before its earliestAvailableSlot (4138816, vs 4105088 on unstable-sas).
